title: Typical polynomial threshold degree bound
statement: For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, choose a uniformly random function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. The probability that $f$ has no polynomial threshold representation of Fourier degree at most $K_n$ is at most $2^{-n}$, where $K_n$ is the floor of $\frac n2+\frac n2\sqrt{\frac{2\log(48n)}{n}}$.
